scenarios.steps: Identify the active planning ticket and pick the next implementation ticket.
scenarios.outcome: Issue 00 is clearly active (in-progress), but issue 05 is simultaneously ready-for-agent while Blocked by issue 00; issue-tracker guidance says blocked issues must not start, creating contradictory scheduling signals.
Dependencies clearly establish 00 → 05 → (06, 07) → 08, with 08 also depending on 06 and 07.

scenarios.steps: Determine unsupported-host behavior and completion legality.
scenarios.outcome: Unsupported hosts enter needs-independent-roles; completion requires registered Host attestations or authenticated maintainer fallback for every missing role. Completion also requires role evidence, gates, postmortem, and unresolved-condition clearance.

scenarios.steps: Determine whether future command names/interfaces must already exist.
scenarios.outcome: It is clear that implementation ticket 05 must document commands, schemas, artifact locations, fallback issuer, and exact transitions before completion; future command names need not exist in this planning seed.

findings.summary: Issue 05 is marked ready-for-agent even though line 7 declares it blocked by issue 00, while issue-tracker.md line 60 says blocked issues must not start. The seed should mark 05 blocked/not-ready until 00 reaches terminal complete, or explicitly define that readiness is prospective.

residualRisks: An agent may claim issue 05 before the planning seed is merged, violating the stated dependency rule.
The dependency graph is clear, but the status vocabulary does not distinguish prospective readiness from currently pickable.
